/-!
# Convergence of the Borwein Series with Sinusoidal Coefficient

*References:*
- [MathWorld, Harmonic Series](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/HarmonicSeries.html)
- Borwein, J.; Bailey, D.; Girgensohn, R. *Experimentation in Mathematics: Computational Paths
  to Discovery*, A K Peters, 2004, p. 56.
-/

namespace BorweinSineSeries

/--
Does the series
$$
  \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{\left(\frac{2}{3} + \frac{1}{3}\sin n\right)^n}{n}
$$
converge?

After computing approximately $10^7$ terms, the partial sums approximate $2.163$.

See https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.11017 for a proof of the convergence,
relying on an irrationality measure for pi.

Also see
https://github.com/AxiomMath/gdm-formal-conjectures/blob/main/docs/BorweinSineSeries.md
for a partial formalization of the conjecture,
conditional on such an irrationality measure of pi (cf https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.06345).
-/
@[category research solved, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/AxiomMath/gdm-formal-conjectures/blob/main/BorweinSineSeries/solution.lean",  AMS 26 40]
theorem borwein_sine_series :
    answer(True) ↔
      Summable fun n : ℕ+ ↦ ((2 / 3 + 1 / 3 * Real.sin (n : ℝ)) ^ (n : ℕ)) / (n : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end BorweinSineSeries

status_issues.recorded: An unconditional formal_proof using lean4 attribute points to AxiomMath's BorweinSineSeries/solution.lean.
status_issues.source_status: The cited artifact proves convergence only under an explicit PiIrrBound hypothesis. It does not supply a proof of that hypothesis. This is a conditional formalization, although the mathematical convergence result is solved and answer(True) is correct.
status_issues.evidence: At https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AxiomMath/gdm-formal-conjectures/main/BorweinSineSeries/solution.lean, lines 8–10 define PiIrrBound as a positive-constant, sufficiently-large-denominator rational-approximation bound for π with exponent 7.10321. Lines 801–804 state `theorem borwein_sine_series (hpi : PiIrrBound) : Summable ...`. The theorem retains this parameter after Lean checking. Boppana's arXiv:2007.11017 independently establishes the unconditional mathematical convergence result.
status_issues.suggested_change: Keep the theorem statement, answer(True), and research solved category unchanged. State the assumed irrationality bound as a research-solved helper declaration and use `conditional formal_proof using lean4 at "..." assuming <bound_declaration>`. Alternatively, omit the formal_proof attribute until an unconditional formal proof is linked.

reformulations.difference: The source asks whether the ordinary partial sums converge; Lean uses Summable over ℕ+, which defaults to unordered summation over finite subsets.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every positive integer n, the base 2/3 + (1/3) sin n lies in [1/3,1], so the summand is positive. Reindexing ℕ+ by k ↦ k+1 and applying hasSum_iff_tendsto_nat_of_nonneg shows that Summable is equivalent to existence of a finite real limit of the ordinary partial sums. answer(True) ↔ Summable reduces to this positive convergence assertion. The exact equivalence with the file's theorem type was proved as Review.ordinary_convergence_iff in /workspace/review/scratch.lean; its axioms contain no sorryAx.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found. Lean checks confirmed real-valued division, the natural-number exponent, strictly positive denominators and summands, and the n=1 and n=2 cases. A floating-point check of 10^7 terms gave approximately 2.162759, consistent with the docstring's 2.163. The linked conditional proof checked without sorryAx after a scratch-only compatibility adjustment allowing one redundant `simp at h` to make no progress. The original book page was not directly accessible; its question is explicitly reproduced in both MathWorld and Boppana's introduction. The authors' errata contain no correction to page 56. All experiments and downloaded artifacts were kept under /workspace/review; no repository source was edited.
